change.problem: A spec containing both :arity and :arities was checked against :arity first, rejecting String.set's supported three-argument form before dispatch.
change.semantics: An explicit :arities set is authoritative; :arity is the fallback only when no set is provided.
change.fixedArityPath: Does not construct a singleton arity set on each call.

coverage: Both three- and four-argument UTF8 setters enter through runtime-prim, with ASCII, multibyte UTF8, NUL, invalid byte positions, and end positions.
Explicit arity sets override a fallback :arity, including rejection of counts outside the set.
Both exact registered String.set ownership/type signatures lower and run on reference, mutable, and demand JVM backends.
Unique, shared, and persistent String ownership and unchanged earlier snapshots are preserved.
Accepting both counts does not weaken ABI ownership/type rejection.
All five multi-arity Nat cast registrations retain their one- and two-argument forms and reject invalid counts.

precedingEquivalentExpressionValidation.reasonReplaced: Semantically equivalent, but constructs a singleton set on common fixed-arity calls.
precedingEquivalentExpressionValidation.scope: This broader result belongs to the preceding expression; it is not reported as validation of the final expression.

reportedLiveAdoption.canary: Three- and four-argument direct dispatch passed with unchanged canary world.
reportedLiveAdoption.source: Root agent's actual adoption report; the implementation agent did not modify the live REPL.

limitations: These are correctness checks and one diagnostic adoption timing, not a performance benchmark.
RSS is sampled and does not establish an exact peak.
No new native oracle generation or Node validation was performed for this validator-only change.
This record does not establish completion of the ordinary macro probe.
